q: Neither the teacher nor the students ___ aware of the change.
e: With neither...nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject. Students is plural, so were is correct.

q: She ___ in Yangon since 2022.
e: Since 2022 is a period continuing to now, so the present perfect has lived is required.

q: When I arrived, they ___ dinner.
e: The dinner was already in progress when I arrived, so the past continuous were having is correct.

q: If I ___ enough money, I would buy a new laptop.
e: This is a second conditional about an unreal present, so the if-clause uses had.

q: The report ___ by the manager yesterday.
e: The report received the action yesterday, so the past passive was written is correct.

q: You ___ wear a helmet when riding a motorcycle.
e: Wearing a helmet is required, so the modal is must.

q: He is the man ___ helped me yesterday.
e: Who is the subject of helped, so the relative pronoun is who.

q: The book ___ I bought yesterday is very useful.
e: The book is a thing, so the relative pronoun is which.

q: I enjoy ___ English novels.
e: Enjoy is followed by the gerund reading.

q: She decided ___ abroad.
e: Decide is followed by to plus the infinitive: to study.

q: The teacher made the students ___ the exercise again.
e: Make someone do something uses the bare infinitive do.

q: My parents allowed me ___ the university.
e: Allow someone to do something uses to enter.

q: He went to the library ___ some books.
e: To borrow gives his purpose: he went to the library in order to borrow books.

q: She was tired, ___ she continued working.
e: Tired and continued working contrast, so the linker is but.

q: ___ it was raining, they continued the match.
e: Although introduces the contrast: they continued even though it was raining.

q: I stayed at home ___ I was sick.
e: Because gives the reason she stayed at home.

q: ___ being tired, he finished the work.
e: Despite is followed by being tired, not by a clause.

q: The boy is ___ intelligent that he can solve the problem easily.
e: The pattern is so + adjective + that: so intelligent that.

q: It was ___ difficult problem that nobody could solve it.
e: Before an adjective and a singular noun, use such a: such a difficult problem.

q: She is old ___ to drive a car.
e: Enough follows the adjective: old enough to drive.

q: He speaks English ___ than his brother.
e: Than requires the comparative better.

q: This is ___ book I have ever read.
e: The superlative of this long adjective is the most interesting.

q: There isn't ___ milk left.
e: Milk is uncountable, so the negative uses much.

q: There are ___ students in the classroom.
e: Students are countable, so many is correct.

q: I have ___ friends in this city, so I don't feel lonely.
e: A few means some friends, which matches not feeling lonely.

q: Neither answer ___ correct.
e: Neither answer is singular, so the verb is is.

q: Each student ___ responsible for his or her work.
e: Each student is singular, so the verb is is.

q: The news ___ surprising.
e: News is a singular noun, so the verb is was.

q: Mathematics ___ my favourite subject.
e: Mathematics is treated as singular, so the verb is is.

q: Hardly ___ the station when the train arrived.
e: Hardly at the start puts the auxiliary before the subject: had I reached.

q: No sooner ___ home than it started to rain.
e: No sooner is followed by had I arrived, and then than.

q: Never ___ such a beautiful place before.
e: Never at the start inverts the present perfect: have I seen.

q: Rarely ___ late for class.
e: Rarely at the start inverts the verb: is he.

q: Only after the examination ___ how difficult it had been.
e: Only after the examination is followed by did I realize.

q: Under no circumstances ___ this door.
e: Under no circumstances inverts the modal: should you open.

q: Not only ___ intelligent, but she is also hardworking.
e: Not only at the start inverts the verb: is she.

q: If I had known the truth, I ___ you.
e: If I had known is a third conditional, so the result is would have told.

q: If he studied harder, he ___ the exam.
e: If he studied is a second conditional, so the result is would pass.

q: If water reaches 100°C, it ___.
e: A general scientific fact uses the present simple: water boils at 100°C.

q: I wish I ___ more time.
e: A wish about the present uses the past form had.

q: I wish I ___ the answer yesterday.
e: A wish about yesterday uses the past perfect had known.

q: She wishes she ___ speak French.
e: A wish about ability uses could.

q: I'd rather you ___ here tonight.
e: Would rather that someone else do something uses the past: stayed.

q: You had better ___ now.
e: Had better is followed by the bare infinitive leave.

q: He used to ___ football when he was young.
e: Used to is followed by the bare infinitive play.

q: She is used to ___ early.
e: Be used to is followed by the gerund waking.

q: I am getting used to ___ alone.
e: Getting used to is followed by the gerund living.

q: You needn't ___ so much food.
e: Needn't is followed by the bare infinitive buy.

q: He needn't have ___ so early.
e: Needn't have is followed by the past participle left.

q: The harder you work, ___ your results will be.
e: The paired comparative is the harder ... the better.

q: The more you practise, ___ you become.
e: The paired comparative is the more ... the more confident.

q: She is ___ honest person.
e: Honest begins with a vowel sound, so the article is an.

q: He plays ___ piano very well.
e: A musical instrument takes the: the piano.

q: Neither John ___ Peter came to the meeting.
e: Neither is completed by nor.

q: Either you ___ your brother must attend the meeting.
e: Either is completed by or.

q: Both the teacher ___ the students were excited.
e: Both is completed by and.

q: She left early ___ she could catch the bus.
e: So that introduces the purpose: she could catch the bus.

q: He spoke quietly ___ disturb the baby.
e: In order not to is followed by the bare infinitive disturb.

q: He talks as if he ___ everything.
e: As if for an unreal comparison uses the past form knew.

q: The word “essential” is closest in meaning to
e: Essential means necessary.

q: “Rapid” means
e: Rapid means sudden and fast.

q: “Accurate” means
e: Accurate means correct.

q: “Reliable” means
e: Reliable means able to be trusted.

q: “Obtain” means
e: In this item, obtain is given the meaning obtain or get.

q: “Prevent” means
e: Prevent means stop something from happening.

q: “Increase” is opposite in meaning to
e: The opposite of increase is decrease.

q: “Ancient” is opposite in meaning to
e: The opposite of ancient is modern.

q: “Generous” is opposite in meaning to
e: The opposite of generous is selfish.

q: “Complex” is closest in meaning to
e: Complex means complicated.

q: The scientist made an important ___.
e: After an adjective, the noun form is discovery.

q: The government wants to ___ pollution.
e: After wants to, the base verb is reduce.

q: Regular exercise is ___ to good health.
e: After is, the adjective form is beneficial.

q: The company is trying to improve its ___.
e: After its, the noun form is efficiency.

q: We need to find a ___ solution to the problem.
e: Before the noun solution, the adjective is practical.

q: He answered the question ___.
e: The verb answered is modified by the adverb confidently.

q: The medicine had a positive ___ on the patient.
e: A positive result is the noun effect, not the verb affect.

q: Lack of sleep can ___ your concentration.
e: Affect is the verb meaning to change or influence concentration.

q: The teacher asked us to ___ attention.
e: The fixed phrase is pay attention.

q: Please ___ a decision before Friday.
e: The fixed phrase is make a decision.

q: He ___ a mistake in the report.
e: The fixed phrase is made a mistake.

q: We should ___ advantage of this opportunity.
e: The fixed phrase is take advantage of.

q: The meeting was ___ because of the storm.
e: Called off means cancelled.

q: Please ___ the lights before leaving.
e: Turn off means switch the lights off.

q: The plane ___ at 8:00 a.m.
e: A plane took off when it left the ground.

q: The word “maintain” means
e: Maintain means keep in good condition.

q: “Significant” means
e: Significant means important.

q: “Consequently” means
e: Consequently means therefore.

q: “Despite” is closest in meaning to
e: Despite means in spite of.

q: “Approximately” means
e: Approximately means roughly.

q:
Choose the part containing the error.

She (A) go to school (B) every day because she (C) wants to learn.
e: She go should be she goes, so part A contains the error.

q:
Choose the part containing the error.

He have finished his homework.
e: He have should be he has, so He have is the error.

q:
Choose the part containing the error.

Neither the teacher nor the students was ready for the examination.
e: The nearer subject is students, which is plural, so was ready is the error.

q:
Choose the part containing the error.

She is interested on learning foreign languages.
e: Interested is followed by in, not on.

q:
Choose the part containing the error.

The teacher suggested to go to the library.
e: Suggest is followed by a gerund, so to go is the error.

q:
Choose the part containing the error.

I look forward to meet you next week.
e: Look forward to is followed by a gerund, so to meet is the error.

q:
Choose the part containing the error.

The information are very useful for students.
e: Information is uncountable, so are is the error.

q:
Choose the part containing the error.

She has lived here since five years.
e: A length of time uses for, so since five years is the error.

q:
Choose the part containing the error.

He is one of the best student in the class.
e: One of the best is followed by a plural noun, so student is the error.

q:
Choose the part containing the error.

This is the book which I bought it yesterday.
e: Which already stands for the book, so the extra it is the error.

q:
Choose the part containing the error.

If I had known about the problem, I would have helped you.
e: The third conditional is formed correctly, so there is no error.

q:
Choose the part containing the error.

Do you know where did he live?
e: An indirect question keeps statement order, so where did he live is the error.

q:
Choose the part containing the error.

Hardly I had arrived when the meeting started.
e: Hardly must invert the subject and auxiliary, so Hardly I had arrived is the error.

q:
Choose the part containing the error.

The box is enough strong to carry the heavy books.
e: Enough comes after the adjective, so is enough strong is the error.

q:
Choose the part containing the error.

She speaks English more fluently than me do.
e: This item's key is No error, so none of the three parts is marked as the mistake.

q:
Choose the part containing the error.

Each of the students have submitted the assignment.
e: Each of the students is singular, so have submitted is the error.

q:
Choose the part containing the error.

The teacher made him to rewrite the answer.
e: Make is followed by a bare infinitive, so to rewrite is the error.

q:
Choose the part containing the error.

He is accustomed to work late at night.
e: Accustomed to is followed by a gerund, so to work is the error.

q:
Choose the part containing the error.

I have seen him yesterday.
e: Yesterday needs the past simple, so have seen is the error.

q:
Choose the part containing the error.

She is senior than me in the company.
e: Senior is followed by to, so than me is the error.

q:
Choose the part containing the error.

Despite of being tired, he continued working.
e: Despite is not followed by of, so Despite of is the error.

q:
Choose the part containing the error.

No sooner had he arrived when the rain started.
e: No sooner is paired with than, so when is the error.

q:
Choose the part containing the error.

She is so intelligent student that everyone admires her.
e: An adjective plus a noun needs such a, so so intelligent student is the error.

q:
Choose the part containing the error.

I would rather stay at home than to go outside.
e: Than after would rather takes a bare infinitive, so than to go is the error.

q:
Choose the part containing the error.

The number of students in this class are increasing.
e: The number of is singular, so are increasing is the error.

q:
Many students believe that studying for long hours is the best way to prepare for an examination. However, the number of hours spent studying does not always determine the quality of learning. Effective study requires concentration, regular revision, adequate sleep and opportunities to practise what has been learned. A student who studies for two focused hours may learn more than someone who spends five hours studying while frequently checking a phone.

What is the main idea of the passage?
a: Students should study five hours every day.
Long study hours always produce better results.
Effective study depends on quality, not simply time.
e: The passage says the quality of study matters more than the number of hours.

q:
Renewable energy comes from sources that can naturally be replaced, such as sunlight, wind and flowing water. Unlike fossil fuels, these sources do not depend on limited reserves underground. Renewable energy can reduce dependence on fossil fuels and may help reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Nevertheless, renewable energy systems can also face challenges, including high initial costs, variable energy production and the need for suitable locations.

What is renewable energy?
e: The passage defines it as energy from sources that can naturally be replaced.

q:
Change into passive voice:

“People speak English all over the world.”
a: English is spoken all over the world.
English was spoken all over the world.
English speaks all over the world.
English has spoken all over the world.
e: The object becomes the subject and the verb becomes the present passive: is spoken.

q:
Change into passive voice:

“They built the bridge last year.”
a: The bridge was built last year.
The bridge is built last year.
The bridge has built last year.
e: Last year needs the past passive: was built.

q:
Change into reported speech:

He said, “I am tired.”
a: He said that I was tired.
He said that he was tired.
He said that he is tired.
e: Am becomes was, and I changes to he.

q:
Change into reported speech:

She said, “I will help you.”
a: She said that she would help me.
She said that I would help her.
She says that she will help me.
She said that she helps me.
e: Will becomes would, and you changes to me.

q:
Rewrite using “because of”:

“He stayed home because he was sick.”
a: He stayed home because of his sickness.
He stayed home because of he was sick.
Because of he sick, he stayed home.
He stayed home because his sickness.
e: Because plus a clause becomes because of plus the noun sickness.

q:
Rewrite using “despite”:

“Although he was tired, he continued working.”
a: Despite he was tired, he continued working.
Despite being tired, he continued working.
Despite of tired, he continued working.
Despite he tired, he continued working.
e: Although he was tired becomes Despite being tired.

q:
Rewrite using “unless”:

“If you do not study, you will fail.”
a: Unless you study, you will fail.
Unless you do not study, you will fail.
e: If you do not study becomes Unless you study.

q:
Rewrite using “too ... to”:

“The box is so heavy that I cannot lift it.”
a: The box is too heavy for me to lift.
The box is very heavy to lift me.
The box is enough heavy to lift.
The box is too heavy that I lift it.
e: So heavy that I cannot lift it becomes too heavy for me to lift.

q:
Rewrite using “enough”:

“He is so strong that he can carry the box.”
a: He is enough strong to carry the box.
He is strong enough to carry the box.
He is so strong enough to carry the box.
He enough is strong to carry the box.
e: So strong that he can becomes strong enough to.

q:
Rewrite using “No sooner”:

“As soon as he arrived, the meeting began.”
a: No sooner he arrived than the meeting began.
No sooner had he arrived than the meeting began.
No sooner did he arrived when the meeting began.
No sooner he had arrived when the meeting began.
e: As soon as he arrived becomes No sooner had he arrived than.

q:
Rewrite using “Hardly”:

“As soon as she sat down, the phone rang.”
a: Hardly she had sat down when the phone rang.
Hardly had she sat down when the phone rang.
Hardly did she sat down than the phone rang.
Hardly she sat down than the phone rang.
e: As soon as she sat down becomes Hardly had she sat down when.

q:
Rewrite using “so ... that”:

“It was such a difficult question that nobody could answer it.”
a: It was so difficult a question that nobody could answer it.
It was so a difficult question that nobody answered it.
It was such difficult that nobody answered it.
It was too difficult question to answer.
e: Such a difficult question becomes so difficult a question.

q:
Rewrite using “such ... that”:

“The movie was so interesting that we watched it twice.”
a: It was such interesting movie that we watched it twice.
It was such an interesting movie that we watched it twice.
It was so an interesting movie that we watched it twice.
It was such a movie interesting that we watched it twice.
e: So interesting becomes such an interesting movie.

q:
Rewrite using “It was ... who”:

“John broke the window.”
a: It was John who broke the window.
It is John who broke the window.
It was John which broke the window.
It was John whom broke the window.
e: It was John who puts the emphasis on John.

q:
Rewrite using “wish”:

“I don't have enough money.”
a: I wish I have enough money.
I wish I had enough money.
I wish I will have enough money.
I wish I am having enough money.
e: A wish about not having money now uses the past: I wish I had.

q:
Rewrite using “used to”:

“When I was young, I played football regularly.”
a: I use to play football regularly.
I used to play football regularly.
I am used to play football regularly.
e: A past habit becomes used to plus the bare infinitive play.

q:

“He talks like he knows everything.”
a: He talks as if he knew everything.
He talks as if he knows everything.
He talks as if he will know everything.
He talks as if knowing everything.
e: As if for something unreal uses the past: knew.

q:

“If you practise more, you become more confident.”
a: The more you practise, the more confident you become.
More you practise, more confident you become.
The more you practise, more confident become you.
The more practising, the confident you become.
